quests.instruction: Which skin on your body is the thinnest, only about half a millimeter thick?
quests.hint: It folds easily every time you blink.
quests.explanation: Eyelid skin is very thin, which helps it fold and move easily, but it also puffs up and bruises easily.
quests.funFact: Thin eyelid skin is why dark circles and puffy eyes show up so easily.

quests.instruction: Veins look bluish through your skin, but what color is the blood inside them?
quests.hint: Think about the color of blood when a nurse draws it.
quests.explanation: Blood is always red. It is a darker red when it carries less oxygen, and the skin around a vein makes it look blue.
quests.funFact: The way light bounces off skin is what makes veins look blue or green.

quests.instruction: The ear has three parts. Which part is the one you can see and touch on the side of your head?
quests.hint: It is shaped like a funnel.
quests.explanation: The outer ear gathers sound and sends it down a short tunnel to the eardrum. The middle ear and inner ear are hidden inside your head.
quests.funFact: The curves of the outer ear help you tell whether a sound is coming from in front of you or behind you.

quests.instruction: People who are called double-jointed do not really have extra joints. What do they have that stretches farther than usual?
quests.hint: They are the bands that hold bones together.
quests.explanation: Some people have looser ligaments, so their joints bend farther than most. They have the same number of joints as everyone else.
quests.funFact: Dancers and gymnasts train for flexibility, but being very bendy is partly something you are born with.

quests.instruction: Which muscles, used for chewing, are among the strongest in your body for their size?
quests.hint: You can feel them bulge near your ears when you clench your teeth.
quests.explanation: Jaw muscles can close your teeth with a lot of force, which helps you chew tough food.
quests.funFact: A grown-up's back teeth can bite down with a force of tens of kilograms.

quests.instruction: Six tiny muscles attached to each eyeball let you look up, down, and side to side. What are they called?
quests.hint: They move the eyeballs, not the lids.
quests.explanation: Eye muscles tilt each eyeball in different directions, and they work together so that both eyes point at the same thing.
quests.funFact: Your eyes can jump from one target to another in about a tenth of a second.

quests.instruction: Which thin strip of skin at the base of a fingernail seals out germs?
quests.hint: It frames the bottom edge of the nail.
quests.explanation: The cuticle forms a seal around the nail's growing base, so pushing, picking, or cutting it can let germs in.
quests.funFact: Healthy nails grow from the area just under the cuticle.

quests.instruction: Which sticky film of germs builds up on teeth and is wiped away by brushing and flossing?
quests.hint: You can feel it as a fuzzy coating if you skip brushing.
quests.explanation: Plaque is a soft layer of germs and food bits that grows on teeth, and brushing and flossing wipe it away.
quests.funFact: Plaque starts to build up again within hours after brushing.

quests.instruction: A toothbrush often misses which spots, so floss is used to clean them?
quests.hint: They are the narrow spaces where teeth touch.
quests.explanation: Floss slides into the narrow spaces where bristles cannot reach and removes food and plaque.
quests.funFact: Floss cleans surfaces that a brush cannot reach at all.

quests.instruction: Trillions of tiny helpful living things in your intestines help you digest food and make some vitamins. What are they called?
quests.hint: They are too small to see without a microscope.
quests.explanation: Gut bacteria help break down food that your body cannot digest alone, and some make vitamins.
quests.funFact: The number of bacteria in and on your body is about the same as the number of your own cells.

quests.instruction: Which organs would float if you put them in water, because they are full of tiny air spaces?
quests.hint: They are soft and spongy.
quests.explanation: Lungs are filled with air sacs, so they are much lighter than other organs and can float.
quests.funFact: Having lungs full of air is part of why you float more easily after a deep breath.

quests.instruction: Behind the eardrum is a small air-filled space with three tiny bones. Which part of the ear is that?
quests.hint: It sits between the eardrum and the cochlea.
quests.explanation: The middle ear passes vibrations from the eardrum along the three tiny bones to the inner ear.
quests.funFact: Middle ear infections are common in children, because the tube that drains the middle ear is short and nearly flat.

quests.instruction: Which part of a hair is alive and growing, while the part you can see is not?
quests.hint: It sits in the follicle under the skin.
quests.explanation: New hair cells are made at the root and pushed upward, and they harden and die as they rise, which is why a haircut does not hurt.
quests.funFact: Pulling a hair hurts because nerves wrap around the root.

quests.instruction: Only about the front sixth of your eyeball shows. Where is the rest hidden?
quests.hint: It is a bony bowl in your skull.
quests.explanation: Each eyeball sits in a bony hollow called a socket, which protects it from bumps.
quests.funFact: Each eye socket is formed by seven different bones.

quests.instruction: Sound travels from the outside into your head through a short tunnel that ends at the eardrum. What is it called?
quests.hint: Earwax is made here.
quests.explanation: The ear canal leads from the outer ear to the eardrum and carries sound along it.
quests.funFact: Whether your earwax is sticky and wet or dry and flaky depends on your genes.

quests.instruction: A grown-up's body holds a certain amount of blood. Which amount is closest?
quests.hint: Think of a few large bottles of water.
quests.explanation: An adult body holds about five liters of blood. A child has less.
quests.funFact: A child's body holds about two to three liters of blood.

quests.instruction: Your mouth is quietly busy making saliva all day long. Which amount is closest to the daily total?
quests.hint: It is a lot more than you would guess.
quests.explanation: Your salivary glands make roughly one to two liters of saliva a day, mostly without you noticing.
quests.funFact: You make less saliva while you sleep, which is one reason morning breath happens.

quests.instruction: Water makes up what share of a grown-up's body weight?
quests.hint: Most of you is made of it.
quests.explanation: Roughly sixty percent of an adult's body is water. In babies, it is closer to seventy-five percent.
quests.funFact: Even your bones contain water.

quests.instruction: Measure a school-age child on each birthday. How much taller are they than last year, usually?
quests.hint: It is less than the length of a pencil.
quests.explanation: Between ages 5 and 12, most children grow about five to six centimeters a year, with faster spurts at some times.
quests.funFact: Most children grow a little faster in spring and summer than in fall and winter.

quests.instruction: Which can a healthy person last longer without: food or water?
quests.hint: One of them is needed within a few days.
quests.explanation: A person can survive only about three days without water, but weeks without food, which is why drinking enough water matters so much.
quests.funFact: A camel's hump stores fat, not water.

quests.instruction: Look straight ahead without moving your head. How wide is the view that your two eyes share?
quests.hint: It is wider than straight ahead, but not all the way around.
quests.explanation: Each eye sees about 150 degrees, and their views overlap in the middle, giving about 200 degrees together.
quests.funFact: A horse's eyes sit on the sides of its head, so it can see almost all the way around.

quests.instruction: Which part of you can notice vibrations from about 20 to 20,000 times each second, from low rumbles to high squeaks?
quests.hint: It turns vibrations into signals.
quests.explanation: Ears can pick up a huge range of pitches, from deep rumbles to high squeaks.
quests.funFact: Dogs can hear sounds much higher than people can.

quests.instruction: Imagine unrolling all of your skin into one flat sheet. What size would it be closest to?
quests.hint: Think of a blanket for one person.
quests.explanation: An adult's skin covers about two square meters, roughly the size of a single-bed sheet.
quests.funFact: A newborn baby's skin covers only about a quarter of a square meter.

quests.instruction: Which organ is the heaviest in your body, weighing more than your liver or your brain?
quests.hint: You wear it on the outside.
quests.explanation: In an adult, the skin weighs about three to four kilograms, more than twice the weight of the brain.
quests.funFact: Children's skin often heals faster than older people's skin.

quests.instruction: Count the hairs on a typical head. Which guess is closest?
quests.hint: It is a number in the hundred thousands.
quests.explanation: Most people have around 100,000 hairs on their scalp.
quests.funFact: On average, people with blond hair have more hairs than people with red hair.

quests.instruction: Take the biggest breath you can. How much air fits in a grown-up's lungs?
quests.hint: A deep breath uses far more than a normal one.
quests.explanation: An adult's lungs can hold about six liters, though an ordinary breath moves only a small part of that.
quests.funFact: Athletes can have a larger lung capacity because of their training.

quests.instruction: A runner trains hard in the heat for an hour. How much sweat can the body make?
quests.hint: That is about a big water bottle.
quests.explanation: Hard exercise in the heat can make a person sweat about a liter in an hour, which is why drinking water matters.
quests.funFact: Sweat is mostly water, with a little salt.

quests.instruction: A tooth snaps off right at the gum line. Which part of the tooth is left in the jaw?
quests.hint: It is the hidden part.
quests.explanation: The crown is the visible part, and the root is anchored in the jawbone, so a break at the gum leaves the root behind.
quests.funFact: A knocked-out adult tooth can sometimes be saved if it is kept in milk and seen by a dentist quickly.

quests.instruction: When sunburned skin peels, the flakes do not hurt, because they are made of which kind of cells?
quests.hint: They are no longer alive.
quests.explanation: The top layer of skin is made of flat cells that have died and act like a shield. Fresh cells below replace them.
quests.funFact: Peeling is the body's way of getting rid of damaged cells.

quests.instruction: Your brain is protected by a hard case and a liquid cushion. Which pair is that?
quests.hint: One is bone, and the other is a watery liquid.
quests.explanation: The skull is the hard case, and a clear fluid around the brain acts like a cushion against bumps.
quests.funFact: The cushioning fluid is replaced several times a day.
